# aos command index

Every public command, grouped, generated from the registry. This is the
complete list; `aos <group> <cmd> --help` has the full flag set, and
`aos commands` says what this particular machine can run right now.
Marks: *display* = needs a desktop session (exit 2 without one);
*blocking* = runs until stopped; *platforms* = only those OSes.

## adapters

Commands you add yourself, without writing a program

### `aos adapters list`

List the adapters this machine has loaded

```bash
aos adapters list [--json]
aos adapters list
```

### `aos adapters path`

Print the directory adapters are read from

```bash
aos adapters path
```

### `aos adapters example`

Print a starter adapter, ready to save and edit

```bash
aos adapters example [--write]
aos adapters example
aos adapters example --write
```


## app

Installed and running applications

### `aos app list`

List installed applications, or only the running ones, with id and path

```bash
aos app list [--running] [--filter=<substring>] [--json]
aos app list
aos app list --running
aos app list --filter=code --json
```

### `aos app hide-others`

Hide (minimize) every app except the frontmost one

```bash
aos app hide-others
```

### `aos app quit-all`

Quit every running app, except those named; asks first unless --yes

```bash
aos app quit-all [--except=<name,name>] [--yes]
aos app quit-all                       # lists what would quit, then asks
aos app quit-all --except="Slack,Visual Studio Code" --yes
```

```bash
aos appearance nightlight    # on | off

```

## batch

Run many aos steps from YAML: in order, or together with parallel

### `aos batch`

Run a YAML list of steps (a file, - for stdin, or the YAML inline); everything is checked first

```bash
aos batch <file.yaml | - | inline yaml> [--check] [--json]
aos batch demo.yaml
aos batch --check demo.yaml
aos batch '[launch: calc, parallel: [say: seven, click: Calculator Seven], type: Notepad done]'
aos batch verbs   # every verb, generated from the commands
```

### `aos batch verbs`

List every verb a batch step can use

```bash
aos batch verbs [--json]
aos batch verbs
aos batch verbs --json
```


## battery

Battery presence and charge

### `aos battery status`

Print battery charge, charging state, and health (capacity, cycles) where reported

```bash
aos battery status [--json]
aos battery status    # 87%  discharging  3:41 remaining  (health 97%, 15 cycles, 30.7°C)
aos battery status --json
```

### `aos battery present`

Exit 0 when a battery is present, 1 otherwise

```bash
aos battery present
aos battery present && echo has a battery
```

### `aos battery percent`

Print the charge percentage as a bare number

```bash
aos battery percent
aos battery percent    # 87
```


## bluetooth

### `aos bluetooth status`

Print whether Bluetooth is present and on

```bash

```

### `aos bluetooth list`



### `aos bluetooth off`

## capture

Screenshots

### `aos capture screenshot`

Take a screenshot

*display · alias: screenshot*

```bash
aos capture screenshot [fullscreen|region|window] [--monitor=<n>] [--region=<x,y,w,h>] [--app=<name>] [--copy] [--out=<path>]
aos screenshot
aos capture screenshot region --copy
aos capture screenshot --monitor=2
aos capture screenshot --app=Chrome --out=/tmp/term.png
aos capture screenshot --region=0,0,800,600
```

### `aos capture qr`

Decode the QR codes in an image file, a screen region or a whole monitor

*display*

```bash
aos capture qr [<image>] [--region=<x,y,w,h>] [--monitor=<n>] [--json]
aos capture qr ticket.png                    # decode a PNG, JPEG or GIF file
aos capture qr --region=100,100,400,400      # decode what is on screen there
aos capture qr --monitor=2 --json            # every QR code on monitor 2, with its bounds
```

### `aos capture text`

OCR a screen region or a whole monitor and print its text in reading order

*display*

```bash
aos capture text [--region=<x,y,w,h>] [--monitor=<n>] [--max-chars=<n>] [--json]
aos capture text --region=100,100,800,400
aos capture text --monitor=2 --json
aos capture text --monitor=1 --region=0,0,600,300   # region relative to monitor 1
# a window's text: aos window text --app=Preview --source=ocr
```

### `aos capture video start`

Start recording the screen with ffmpeg (detached; ask the person first)

*display*

```bash
aos capture video start [smart|monitor|window|region|app|mouse] [--monitor=<n>] [--app=<name>|--title=<s>] [--region=<x,y,w,h>] [--fps=30] [--audio=none|mic|system|both] [--mic=<name|index>] [--zoom=2] [--out=<path.mp4>] [--max=10m] [--indicator=false] [--json]
aos capture video start smart --audio=mic --out=~/Movies/demo.mp4
aos capture video start monitor --monitor=2
aos capture video start mouse --zoom=2
aos capture video start app --app=Chrome
aos capture video start window --app=Terminal
aos capture video start region --region=0,0,1280,720 --max=2m
# exit 2 when ffmpeg (or a loopback device for --audio=system) is missing
```

### `aos capture video stop`

Stop recording, finalize the mp4 and render <out>.final.mp4 with the auto camera

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos capture video stop [--raw] [--json]
aos capture video stop
aos capture video stop --raw --json
```

### `aos capture video status`

Is a recording running, and where is it going

*display*

```bash
aos capture video status [--json]
aos capture video status
```

### `aos capture video mark`

Add a labelled event to the recording (a camera target with --rect)

*display*

```bash
aos capture video mark <label...> [--rect=<x,y,w,h>]
aos capture video mark "login works"
aos capture video mark "the chart" --rect=200,150,800,450
```

### `aos capture video focus`

Point the camera at a place until unfocus (or --hold)

*display*

```bash
aos capture video focus (--rect=<x,y,w,h> | --at=<x,y> [--size=640x360] | --app=<name>|--title=<s> [--find=<text> [--role=<r>]]) [--hold=<duration>] [--zoom=<factor>]
aos capture video focus --rect=100,100,800,450
aos capture video focus --at=640,400 --size=800x450 --hold=4s
aos capture video focus --app=Chrome --find="Sign in" --zoom=2
```

### `aos capture video unfocus`

Send the camera back to its automatic mode

*display*

```bash
aos capture video unfocus
```

### `aos capture video follow`

Switch the live camera: follow the mouse, an app, smart, or off

*display*

```bash
aos capture video follow mouse|app|smart|off [--app=<name>|--title=<s>]
aos capture video follow mouse
aos capture video follow app --app=Chrome
aos capture video follow off
```

### `aos capture video devices`

List the screens, microphones and system-audio sources ffmpeg can record

*display*

```bash
aos capture video devices [--json]
aos capture video devices
```

### `aos capture video zoom`

Re-render an aos recording with the auto camera, from its events file

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos capture video zoom <in.mp4> [--events=<file>] [--out=<file>] [--pad=0.15] [--max-zoom=2.5] [--ease=0.6] [--hold-wide=1.0] [--zoom=2] [--follow=mouse|app|smart|off] [--size=1920x1080] [--json]
aos capture video zoom ~/Movies/demo.mp4
aos capture video zoom demo.mp4 --max-zoom=2 --ease=0.8 --out=demo.cut.mp4
aos capture video zoom demo.mp4 --follow=off
```


## clipboard

Read and write the system clipboard

### `aos clipboard copy`

Copy stdin, or the given words, to the clipboard

```bash
aos clipboard copy [text...]
echo hello | aos clipboard copy
aos clipboard copy "some text"
```

### `aos clipboard paste`

Print the clipboard to stdout

```bash
aos clipboard paste
aos clipboard paste > note.txt
```

### `aos clipboard history`

List the texts the history recorder saw, newest first

```bash
aos clipboard history [--limit=<n>] [--json]
aos clipboard history
aos clipboard history --limit=5 --json
```

### `aos clipboard history start`

Start recording clipboard history in the background (opt-in; ask the person first)

```bash
aos clipboard history start
```

### `aos clipboard history stop`

Stop the clipboard history recorder (the history is kept)

```bash
aos clipboard history stop
```

### `aos clipboard history status`

Say whether the history recorder is running and how much it holds

```bash
aos clipboard history status [--json]
aos clipboard history status
```

### `aos clipboard history get`

Print history entry <n> (1 is the newest)

```bash
aos clipboard history get <n>
aos clipboard history get 2
```

### `aos clipboard history restore`

Put history entry <n> back on the clipboard (1 is the newest)

```bash
aos clipboard history restore <n>
aos clipboard history restore 2
```

### `aos clipboard history clear`

Delete the recorded clipboard history

```bash
aos clipboard history clear
```

## disk

Volumes: free and total space, eject removable drives

### `aos disk list`

List mounted volumes with total, used and free space

```bash
aos disk list [--json]
aos disk list
aos disk list --json
```

### `aos disk usage`

Print total, used and free space of the volume holding a path

```bash
aos disk usage [<path>] [--json]
aos disk usage              # the volume holding your home folder
aos disk usage /Volumes/USB --json
aos disk usage D:\
```

### `aos disk eject`

Unmount and eject a removable volume, by mount point or device

```bash
aos disk eject <mount|device>
aos disk eject /Volumes/USB
aos disk eject /dev/sdb1
aos disk eject E:
```

### `aos disk top`

Rank the biggest folders (and files) under a path, tagging caches, trash and other known space hogs

```bash
aos disk top [<path>] [--depth=<n>] [--limit=<n>] [--timeout=<dur>] [--files] [--json]
aos disk top                      # biggest folders in your home, 5 s budget
aos disk top ~/Library --depth=2 --limit=30
aos disk top ~/Downloads --files --json
aos disk top / --timeout=30s --json
```


## display

Attached monitors

### `aos display brightness`

Print or set a monitor's brightness 0-100: built-in panel or external over DDC/CI (default: the focused window's monitor)

*display*

```bash
aos display brightness [<monitor id>] [<0-100>|+<n>|-<n>] [--monitor=<id>] [--all] [--list] [--json]
aos display brightness            # BenQ GW2785TC (2): 64
aos display brightness +20        # brighter on the focused window's monitor
aos display brightness 2 50       # monitor 2 to 50
aos display brightness --monitor=3
aos display brightness --all 40
aos display brightness --list
aos display brightness -10 --json
```

### `aos display of`

Print the monitor an app's or a window's window is on: id, name and brightness

*display*

```bash
aos display of --app=<name> | --window=<id> [--json]
aos display of --app Safari          # 2  BenQ GW2785TC  brightness 64
aos display of --window 12345 --json
```

### `aos display list`

List attached monitors with geometry and focus state

*display · alias: monitors*

```bash
aos display list
```

### `aos display active`

Print the ID of the monitor the pointer is on

*display*

```bash
aos display active
aos capture screenshot --monitor=$(aos display active)
```

### `aos display focused`

Print the ID of the monitor holding the frontmost window

*display*

```bash
aos display focused
aos window move Chrome --monitor=$(aos display focused)
```

### `aos display modes`

List the resolutions and refresh rates a monitor supports

*display*

```bash
aos display modes <monitor id> [--json]
aos display modes 1
aos display modes 2 --json
```

### `aos display mode`

Switch a monitor to a resolution (highest refresh unless @Hz is given)

*display*

```bash
aos display mode <monitor id> <WxH[@Hz]>
aos display mode 2 2560x1440
aos display mode 1 1920x1080@60
```

### `aos display mirror`

Mirror every monitor to the main one (on) or extend the desktop (off)

*display*

```bash
aos display mirror on|off
aos display mirror on
aos display mirror off
```

## draw

Point at something on screen with a big arrow and a sign

### `aos draw`

Draw a click-through arrow + sign at a point, region, window, text or the mouse

*display*

```bash
aos draw (--at=<x,y> | --rect=<x,y,w,h> | <app> | --app=<name> | --title=<s> | --mouse) [--find=<text> [--role=<r>] [--source=<s>] [--exact] [--nth=<n>]] --text=<sign> [--style=arrow|ring|box] [--shape=bend|straight|zigzag|spiral] [--size=S|M|L] [--color=<name|#hex>] [--from=<side>] [--monitor=<n>] [--position=<side>] [--duration=<seconds>] [--detach] [--animate=on|off] [--preview=<out.png>] [--json]
aos draw --app=Calculator --find=7 --style=ring --text="press 7"
aos draw --at=640,400 --text="click here" --duration=5
aos draw --rect=100,100,400,200 --style=box --text="this area" --preview=/tmp/draw.png
aos draw --mouse --text="you are here" --detach
aos draw stop
# exit 3 when --find does not find the window or the text
```

### `aos draw text`

Show a styled text label (no arrow) inside a window, a monitor, a rect, or beside a point

*display*

```bash
aos draw text <text...> [--app=<name> | --title=<s> | --monitor=<n> | --rect=<x,y,w,h> | --at=<x,y> | --mouse] [--position=bottom-center|top-center|center|left|right|top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right] [--margin=<px|N%>] [--offset=<dx,dy>] [--color=<text colour>] [--bg=auto|none|<colour>] [--font=<name>] [--font-scale=<k>] [--size=S|M|L|XL] [--weight=regular|bold] [--align=left|center|right] [--max-width=<px|N%>] [--duration=<seconds>] [--detach] [--preview=<out.png>] [--json]
aos draw text "Step 2: pick a file" --app=Finder --position=top --color=amber
aos draw text "Done ✓" --monitor=2 --position=center --size=XL --color=green
aos draw text "Line one\nLine two" --rect=100,100,800,500 --position=bottom-right --bg=none
# default: bottom-center of the focused monitor (the recording's monitor while `capture video` runs), subtitle safe area (8% bottom, 5% sides)
```

### `aos draw stop`

Remove every detached drawing

*display*

```bash
aos draw stop [--json]
aos draw stop
```

### `aos draw config`

Show the draw defaults file, or create it with --init

*display*

```bash
aos draw config [--init] [--force]
aos draw config
aos draw config --init
```

### `aos draw fonts`

List the font names --font accepts

*display*

```bash
aos draw fonts
```


## exec

Run commands, with output streamed or captured

### `aos exec run`

Run a command with its output streamed to this terminal

```bash
aos exec run <command> [args...]
aos exec run git status
```

### `aos exec capture`

Run a command and print stdout, stderr, and exit code as JSON

```bash
aos exec capture <command> [args...]
aos exec capture git status
aos exec capture -- ls -la
```

### `aos exec shell`

Run a command line through the platform shell

```bash
aos exec shell <script>
aos exec shell "git log --oneline | head -5"
```


## file

Read, write, and inspect files

### `aos file read`

Print a file, optionally a line range

```bash
aos file read <path> [--lines=<from>:<to>]
aos file read go.mod
aos file read main.go --lines=10:40
```

### `aos file write`

Write stdin, or the given words, to a file

```bash
aos file write <path> [text...]
aos file write notes.txt "first line"
cat in.txt | aos file write out.txt
```

### `aos file append`

Append stdin, or the given words, to a file

```bash
aos file append <path> [text...]
aos file append log.txt "done"
```

### `aos file list`

List a directory

```bash
aos file list [path] [--all] [--json]
aos file list
aos file list ~/Downloads --json
```

### `aos file stat`

Print one path's size, mode, and modified time

```bash
aos file stat <path> [--json]
aos file stat go.mod --json
```

### `aos file mkdir`

Create a directory, including parents

```bash
aos file mkdir <path>
aos file mkdir ~/.config/aos/layouts
```

### `aos file copy`

Copy a file

```bash
aos file copy <source> <destination>
aos file copy a.txt b.txt
```

### `aos file move`

Move or rename a path

```bash
aos file move <source> <destination>
aos file move old.txt new.txt
```

### `aos file delete`

Delete a file, or a directory with --recursive

```bash
aos file delete <path> [--recursive]
aos file delete /tmp/scratch --recursive
```

### `aos file search`

Find files and folders by name, through the OS index when there is one

```bash
aos file search <query> [--root=<dir>] [--kind=file|dir] [--limit=<n>] [--engine=auto|everything|index|walk] [--json]
aos file search invoice --limit=10
aos file search "*.pdf" --root=~/Downloads --json
aos file search notes --kind=dir --engine=walk
```

### `aos file recent`

List recently opened documents, newest first, from the OS's own recents

```bash
aos file recent [--app=<name>] [--limit=<n>] [--json]
aos file recent
aos file recent --app=textedit --limit=5
aos file recent --json
```

## key

Keystrokes and typed text

### `aos key type`

Type text; with --app/--title it goes to that window without needing focus

*display*

```bash
aos key type <text...> [--app=<name>|--title=<substring> [--verify] [--focus] [--json]] [--tab=<title|index|id>] [--force]
aos key type "hello world"
aos key type "hello" --app=TextEdit --verify   # posted to the app, read back from its text field
aos key type "hello" --app=Chrome --focus      # real focus + verify, focus handed back after
# exit 1 if --verify cannot see the text arrive; exit 3 if no window matches
```

### `aos key press`

Press a key combination

*display*

```bash
aos key press <combo> [--app=<name>|--title=<substring> [--focus] [--json]] [--force]
aos key press cmd+shift+s
aos key press enter --app=TextEdit   # posted to the app, no focus change
```

## menu

## say

Speak text aloud with the machine's built-in voices, shown as a subtitle while it plays

### `aos say`

Speak text aloud (or render it to an mp3/wav/aiff); --async returns at once

*platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos say <text...> [--voice=<name>] [--rate=<words per minute>] [--out=<file.mp3|.wav|.aiff>] [--no-subtitle] [--async] [--json] [-- <command...> [--then-wait=false]] [any `subtitle show` style flag: --position --size --color --bg --font --weight --align --max-width --margin --app/--title ...]
aos say "Now I open Notepad and type the note" -- aos key type --app=Notepad "hello"   # speak AND act, wait for both
aos say "build finished"
aos say "Hello there" --voice=Samantha --rate=190
aos say "welcome to the demo" --out=~/Desktop/welcome.mp3
aos say "now I open the settings" --async   # keeps talking while the script goes on
aos say wait
# the text is shown as a subtitle while it is spoken, cleared when it ends; --no-subtitle turns that off
aos say "Saving the report now" --position=top-center --size=L --app=Notepad   # caption style: the subtitle show flags
# long text is captioned a sentence (or clause, ~2 lines) at a time, each timed to its own audio
```

### `aos say voices`

List the installed voices

*platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos say voices [--json]
aos say voices
aos say voices --json
```

### `aos say wait`

Block until every queued and playing `say --async` has finished

*platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash

aos say wait
aos say wait --timeout=30
```

### `aos say stop`

Stop speaking now and drop anything queued

*platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos say stop
```

## tab

Browser and terminal tabs: list, focus, open, send, close

### `aos tab list`

List the tabs of every browser and terminal window

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab list [--app=<name>] [--kind=browser|terminal|editor|files|other] [--window=<aos window id>] [--json]
aos tab list
aos tab list --kind=browser --json
aos tab list --app=Ghostty
```

### `aos tab focus`

Raise a tab's window and select the tab

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab focus (--title=<substring> | --url=<substring> | --cwd=<substring> | --id=<tab id>) [--app=<name>] [--kind=<kind>] [--exact]
aos tab focus --url=github.com/muthuishere/aos/pulls
aos tab focus --title=Inbox --app=Chrome
aos tab focus --cwd=aos --kind=terminal
# exit 3 when no tab matches
```

### `aos tab open`

Open a browser tab on a URL, or a terminal tab in a folder, in the background (--focus to bring it forward)

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab open [<url>] --app=<name> [--window=<id> | --new-window] [--cwd=<dir>] [--command=<cmd>] [--title=<t>] [--wt-window=<name>] [--focus] [--background]
aos tab open https://example.com --app=Chrome
aos tab open https://example.com --app=Safari --new-window
aos tab open --app=Ghostty --cwd=~/src/aos --command="task check"
aos tab open https://example.com --app=Chrome --focus   # raise the window and show the new tab
# default is background: no window raise, no app activation; --background is accepted and does nothing extra
aos tab open --app=WindowsTerminal --wt-window=agents --title=build --cwd=C:\\src   # Windows: named WT window
```

### `aos tab send`

Type text or press a key in a terminal tab without focusing it

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab send --id=<tab id> (--text=<text> | --key=<combo>) [--expect-title=<substring>]
aos tab send --id=ghostty:tab-group-8039faee0:tab-802a71200 --text="ls -la"
aos tab send --id=ghostty:tab-group-8039faee0:tab-802a71200 --key=enter
aos tab send --id=iterm:31:1 --key=ctrl+c
```

### `aos tab close`

Close one tab (never the whole window)

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab close (--id=<tab id> | --title=<substring> | --url=<substring>) [--app=<name>] [--kind=<kind>] [--exact] [--expect-title=<substring>]
aos tab close --id=chrome:1658108662:1658109078
aos tab close --title=example --app=Chrome
aos tab close --id=safari:22718:2 --expect-title=Example
# exit 3 when no tab matches, 4 when several do (name one with --id)
```

### `aos tab read`

Read a browser tab's page as markdown, with refs for its buttons, links and fields

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab read (--id=<tab id> | --url=<substring> | --title=<substring>) [--app=<name>] [--md | --json] [--focus]
aos tab read --id=chrome:1658108662:1658109078
aos tab read --url=web.whatsapp.com --json
# never switches tabs or raises a window: a tab its window is not showing is refused (exit 3);
# run `aos tab focus` on it first, or add --focus to let this command switch to it
# [e7] Message (textarea, empty)   [e8] Send (button)
```

### `aos tab type`

Type into a field of a browser tab's page without taking focus

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab type (--id=<tab id> | --url=<substring> | --title=<substring>) [--app=<name>] (--element=<ref> | --into=<label>) --text=<text> [--enter] [--exact] [--nth=<n>] [--allow-newline] [--allow-focus] [--focus]
aos tab type --id=chrome:1658108662:1658109078 --element=e7 --text="hello" --enter
aos tab type --url=web.whatsapp.com --into="Type a message" --text="hello" --enter
# exit 3 when no field matches, the page changed or focus moved; 4 when several fields match
```

### `aos tab click`

Press a button or link in a browser tab's page, without moving the mouse

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab click (--id=<tab id> | --url=<substring> | --title=<substring>) [--app=<name>] (--element=<ref> | --find=<label>) [--role=button|link|checkbox|radio|...] [--exact] [--nth=<n>] [--allow-focus] [--focus]
aos tab click --id=chrome:1658108662:1658109078 --element=e8
aos tab click --title="Telegram" --find=Send --role=button
# exit 3 when nothing matches or the page changed, 4 when several elements match
```

## watch

Follow what changes on this machine, one JSON line per event

### `aos watch tab`

Print a JSON line with the new text whenever a browser tab's page changes

*display · blocking · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos watch tab (--id=<tab id> | --url=<substring> | --title=<substring>) [--app=<name>] [--match=<text> | --gone=<text>] [--near=<anchor text>] [--exact] [--reload=<duration>] [--interval=<1s>] [--timeout=<duration>] [--max=<n>] [--focus]
aos watch tab --id=chrome:1658108662:1658109078
aos watch tab --url=web.whatsapp.com --match="Build finished" --timeout=5m
aos watch tab --url=example.com/slots --reload=30s --match="Book now" && aos tab click --url=example.com/slots --find="Book now"
aos watch tab --url=example.com/order --reload=1m --gone="Out of stock" --timeout=2h
aos watch tab --url=example.com/item --near="Price" --match="$" --reload=5m
# with --match / --gone: exit 0 when the condition is met, 3 on --timeout or when the tab closes
```

### `aos watch clipboard`

Print a JSON line whenever the clipboard text changes

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch clipboard [--interval=<500ms>] [--max=<n>] [--content]
aos watch clipboard
aos watch clipboard --max=1 --content
```

### `aos watch window`

Print a JSON line whenever the focused window changes, or wait for text to appear or vanish in a window

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch window [--interval=<500ms>] [--max=<n>] | (--app=<name> | --title=<substring>) (--match=<text> | --gone=<text>) [--exact] [--new] [--interval=<2s>] [--timeout=<duration>] [--source=auto|accessibility|ocr] [--json]
aos watch window
aos watch window --max=1
aos watch window --app=Teams --match="Muthu" --timeout=1h && echo "message arrived"
aos watch window --app=Slack --match=deploy --new --json
aos watch window --app=Notes --gone="Syncing" --timeout=2m
# text mode reads the window like `window text`; exit 0 when met, 3 on --timeout; never raises or moves the window
```

### `aos watch file`

Print a JSON line whenever a file or directory entry changes

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch file <path> [--interval=<500ms>] [--max=<n>] [--recursive]
aos watch file ~/Downloads
aos watch file ./notes.md --max=1
aos watch file ./src --recursive --interval=1s
```

### `aos watch battery`

Wait for a battery level or charging state, or print a JSON line for each power change

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch battery [--below=<pct>] [--above=<pct>] [--until=charging|discharging|full] [--interval=<5s>] [--timeout=<dur>] [--json]
aos watch battery --below=20 && echo time to save work      # exit 0 once the charge is under 20%
aos watch battery --until=full --timeout=3h                 # exit 3 if it is not full in 3 hours
aos watch battery --until=discharging                       # exit 0 when the charger is pulled
aos watch battery                                           # a JSON line for plugged, unplugged, full and each % change
```

### `aos watch device`

Report when a USB drive, audio device or Bluetooth device is connected or removed

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch device [--kind=volume|audio|bluetooth[,...]] [--until=added|removed] [--interval=<2s>] [--timeout=<duration>] [--json]
aos watch device
aos watch device --kind=volume --until=added --timeout=2m
aos watch device --kind=audio,bluetooth --json
aos watch device --kind=bluetooth --until=removed && echo 'headphones dropped, pause the music'
# with --until: exit 0 on the first matching event, 3 on --timeout
```

### `aos watch display`

Wait for a monitor to be plugged in or removed, or print a JSON line for each

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch display [--until=added|removed|<count>] [--interval=<2s>] [--timeout=<dur>] [--json]
aos watch display --until=added && aos window move Chrome --monitor=2   # exit 0 when a monitor appears
aos watch display --until=removed --timeout=10m                         # exit 3 if none is unplugged in 10m
aos watch display --until=2                                             # exit 0 once exactly 2 monitors are attached
aos watch display                                                       # a JSON line per monitor added or removed
```

### `aos watch idle`

Exit 0 once the person has been idle for a while, or as soon as they are active again

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch idle (--for=<duration> | --active) [--interval=<1s>] [--timeout=<duration>] [--json]
aos watch idle --for=10m && echo "away from the desk"
aos watch idle --active --timeout=1h   # block until the next key press or mouse move
aos watch idle --for=5m --json
# idle time is input idle: macOS HIDIdleTime, Windows GetLastInputInfo, Linux xprintidle (X11 only)
# exit 0 when met, 3 on --timeout, 1 when this machine cannot report idle time
```

### `aos watch lock`

Print a JSON line when the screen locks or unlocks and when the machine sleeps or wakes

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch lock [--until=locked|unlocked|sleep|wake] [--interval=<1s>] [--timeout=<duration>] [--max=<n>]
aos watch lock
aos watch lock --until=unlocked --timeout=2h && echo "the person is back"
aos watch lock --until=locked
aos watch lock --until=wake --timeout=8h
# lock: macOS CGSession, Windows WTS session state. sleep: seen as a gap in the poll clock, so sleep and wake are reported together on resume (sleep carries slept_ms)
# --until exits 0 when that state is reached (at once if already locked/unlocked), 3 on --timeout
```

### `aos watch network`

Print a JSON line when the machine goes online or offline or changes Wi-Fi network

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch network [--until=online|offline] [--timeout=<duration>] [--max=<n>] [--interval=<5s>]
aos watch network
aos watch network --until=online --timeout=10m && aos exec -- git push
aos watch network --until=offline
# --until: exit 0 when that state is reached (at once if already there), 3 on --timeout
```

### `aos watch camera`

Report when any app starts or stops using the camera

*display · blocking · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos watch camera [--until=busy|free] [--interval=<1s>] [--timeout=<duration>] [--json]
aos watch camera
aos watch camera --until=busy --timeout=10m
aos watch camera --until=free && echo 'call is over, start the build'
aos watch camera --json
# with --until: exit 0 when the state is reached (at once if it already is), 3 on --timeout
```

### `aos watch mic`

Report when any app starts or stops using the microphone

*display · blocking · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos watch mic [--until=busy|free] [--interval=<1s>] [--timeout=<duration>] [--json]
aos watch mic
aos watch mic --until=free --timeout=1h
aos watch mic --until=busy && echo 'someone is on a call'
aos watch mic --json
# with --until: exit 0 when the state is reached (at once if it already is), 3 on --timeout
```

### `aos watch process`

Wait for one process to end or appear, or print a JSON line for each start and stop

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch process --name=<name> | --pid=<n> [--exit | --start] [--interval=<1s>] [--timeout=<dur>] [--json]
aos watch process --name=ffmpeg --exit && echo render done   # exit 0 when ffmpeg ends
aos watch process --pid=4821 --exit --timeout=30m            # exit 3 if it is still running after 30m
aos watch process --name=Xcode --start                       # exit 0 when Xcode appears
aos watch process --name=node                                # a JSON line per start and stop
```

### `aos watch url`

Poll a URL over plain HTTP and report when its text changes, appears or goes away

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch url <url> [--every=<1m>] [--match=<text> | --gone=<text>] [--exact] [--timeout=<duration>] [--max=<n>]
aos watch url https://example.com/status
aos watch url https://example.com/release --every=5m --match="v2.0" --timeout=12h && aos open https://example.com/release
aos watch url https://shop.example.com/item --every=10m --gone="Out of stock"
# with --match / --gone: exit 0 when the condition is met, 3 on --timeout
# pages that need a login or JavaScript: use `aos watch tab`
```


## webapp

Open a site as a standalone browser window

### `aos webapp open`

Open a URL in a chromeless app window

*display*

```bash
aos webapp open <url>
aos webapp open https://app.slack.com
```


## window

Desktop windows: list, focus, move, resize, arrange

### `aos window desktop`

Show the desktop (toggle: run again to bring the windows back)

*display*

```bash
aos window desktop
```

### `aos window list`

List open windows

*display*

```bash
aos window list [--app=<name>] [--title=<substring>] [--kind=browser|terminal|editor|files|other] [--json]
aos window list
aos window list --app=Chrome
aos window list --kind=terminal
```

### `aos window focus`

Bring a window to the front

*display*

```bash
aos window focus <app> | --app=<name> | --title=<substring> [--force]
aos window focus Chrome
# polite: exit 5 when someone used the machine in the last 5s; --force overrides
```

### `aos window move`

Move a window to a zone, a split, or absolute bounds

*display*

```bash
aos window move <app> (--zone=<1A|2:1> | --at=<x,y,w,h>) [--monitor=<n>]
aos window move Chrome --zone=1B
aos window move Chrome --monitor=2 --zone=1:3
aos window move Slack --at=0,25,1920,1055
```

### `aos window resize`

Resize a window in place

*display*

```bash
aos window resize <app> --w=<width> --h=<height>
aos window resize Chrome --w=900 --h=700
```

### `aos window wait`

Wait for a window to appear, then print it

*display*

```bash
aos window wait <app> [--timeout=<ms>]
aos window wait Chrome --timeout=5000
```

### `aos window zones`

Show what each zone means on a real monitor

*display*

```bash
aos window zones [--monitor=<n>] [--show]
aos window zones
aos window zones --monitor=2
aos window zones --show --app=Chrome
```

### `aos window arrange`

Apply a saved layout of many windows in one pass

*display*

```bash
aos window arrange <layout.json | ->
aos window arrange ~/.config/aos/layouts/work.json
echo '[{"app":"Google Chrome","zone":"1A"},{"app":"Slack","zone":"1B"}]' | aos window arrange -
```

### `aos window save`

Save the current layout to a file `window arrange` can apply

*display*

```bash
aos window save <layout.json> [--app=<name>] [--monitor=<n>]
aos window save ~/.config/aos/layouts/work.json
aos window save ~/work.json --app=Chrome
aos window save ~/second-screen.json --monitor=2
```

### `aos window text`

Print all the text of a window, in reading order (accessibility, OCR fallback)

*display*

```bash
aos window text (<app> | --app=<name> | --title=<substring> | --id=<window id> | --focused) [--source=auto|accessibility|ocr] [--json] [--plain] [--max-chars=<n>] [--timeout=<ms>] [--raise]
aos window text TextEdit
aos window text --focused --max-chars=4000
aos window text --app=Chrome --json
aos window text --id=12345 --source=ocr --raise   # OCR a covered window: brings it to the front, then hands focus back
# auto reads the accessibility tree (AX / UI Automation / AT-SPI) and falls back to OCR when it has almost no text
# exit 3 when no window matches
```
